# Internal contracts (Crate / Trait)

Birnio is a desktop app with no HTTP server; the "contract" here is the set of
stable public APIs between crates. Implementers read this before changing code;
the reviewer validates the diff against it.

## birnio-core — domain model

Public types (all `Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq + Serialize + Deserialize`):

- `Request { id: Uuid, name: String, method: HttpMethod, url: Url, headers: Vec<Header>, body: Body, auth: Auth }`
  - `Request::new(name, method, url) -> CoreResult<Self>` — validates the URL;
    errors with `CoreError::InvalidUrl` if `Url::parse` fails. Generates a v4 `id`,
    empty headers, `Body::Empty`, `Auth::None`.
- `HttpMethod` = Get|Post|Put|Patch|Delete|Head|Options. `as_str() -> &'static str`.
- `Header { name: String, value: String, enabled: bool }`.
- `Body` = `Empty` | `Text(String)` | `Json(serde_json::Value)`.
- `Response { status: u16, headers: Vec<Header>, body: Vec<u8>, elapsed: Duration }`.
- `Collection { id, name, nodes: Vec<RequestNode> }`; `Collection::new(name)`.
- `RequestNode` = `Folder { id, name, children }` | `Request(Request)`.
- `Environment`, `Variable { name, value, enabled, secret }`.
- `Auth` = `None` | `Basic(BasicAuth)` | `Bearer(BearerAuth)`.
- Errors: `CoreError` (`InvalidUrl(String)`), alias `CoreResult<T>`.

**Invariants:** `Request.url` is always a valid `Url` (fallible construction). The
domain layer does not depend on HTTP/DB/UI.

## birnio-http — execution

```rust
pub trait HttpExecutor {
    fn execute(&self, request: &Request)
        -> impl Future<Output = HttpResult<Response>> + Send;
}
```

- `ReqwestExecutor::new(client: HttpClient) -> Self` — the concrete implementation.
- `execute` contract: builds a `reqwest::Request` from the domain `Request`
  (method, url, enabled headers, body, auth), executes it, and converts back into
  a `Response` measuring `elapsed` (wall clock via `Instant`). Errors:
  `HttpError::RequestBuild(String)` during build, `HttpError::Reqwest(_)` during
  execution. Alias `HttpResult<T>`.
- `HttpClient::new() -> HttpResult<Self>` — wrapper over `reqwest::Client` with a
  60s timeout, up to 10 redirects, rustls-tls.

**Semantic contract:** `execute` persists nothing and does not interpret the body
beyond transporting it; mapping domain↔reqwest is the exclusive responsibility of
this crate.

## birnio-storage — persistence

- `connect(...) -> StorageResult<DbPool>`, `run_migrations(&DbPool) -> StorageResult<()>`.
- Repositories (async), one module per aggregate:
  - `collections::{ upsert(&DbPool, &Collection) -> StorageResult<()>, get(&DbPool, Uuid) -> StorageResult<Option<Collection>>, list(&DbPool) -> StorageResult<Vec<Collection>> }`
  - `environments::{ upsert, get }`
  - `requests::{ upsert, get }`
- `models/*` convert domain↔record via `from_domain(&T) -> StorageResult<Record>`
  and `into_domain(self) -> StorageResult<T>`.
- Errors: `StorageError` (`#[from]` of `sqlx::Error`, `MigrateError`,
  `serde_json::Error`, `uuid::Error`), alias `StorageResult<T>`.

**Semantic contract:** `upsert` is idempotent by `id` (`ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE`).
JSON serialization is a storage-layer detail; the domain does not know about it.

> M2/M3 swap the implementation for a HAR workspace (see [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md)).
> The repository signatures should stay stable for the rest of the app.

## birnio-import — adapters

- `postman::import(...) -> ImportResult<Collection>` — today extracts only
  `info.name`.
- `bruno::import`, `insomnia::import` — return `ImportError::UnsupportedFormat`.
- Errors: `ImportError` (`UnsupportedFormat(&'static str)`, `Json(#[from])`),
  alias `ImportResult<T>`.

**Semantic contract:** every importer takes external bytes/JSON and returns a
domain `Collection` — with no disk I/O side effects.

## birnio-ui-gtk — UI boundary

No business logic. Each feature follows the quartet `component.rs` (builds
widgets) / `message.rs` (events as an enum) / `state.rs` (feature state) /
`mod.rs` (re-exports). The UI consumes the contracts above (`HttpExecutor`,
repositories) through a services layer (`src/services/`).
